ambiguities.text: The relationship between EIP-7495 and EIP-7916 (progressive Merkle trees) is not fully specified in terms of implementation order.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume EIP-7916 defines the underlying progressive Merkle tree structure and EIP-7495 defines the container-level semantics built on top of it.

ambiguities.text: The specification mentions 'max 256 bits' for active_fields but doesn't clarify handling of larger containers if needed in future.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume 256 is a hard protocol limit and containers requiring more fields would need a different mechanism or type.

implicit_assumptions.description: Verifiers trust that the active_fields bitvector accurately represents which fields are present in the container.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A forged active_fields could allow an attacker to create colliding hashes for containers with different field configurations.

implicit_assumptions.description: Light clients and smart contracts have access to the correct container schema definition to interpret active_fields.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Verifiers with outdated schemas may misinterpret proofs or reject valid containers.

implicit_assumptions.description: The hash function used for Merkleization (SHA256 or similar) is collision-resistant.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Hash collisions could allow attackers to forge Merkle proofs for arbitrary field values.

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot manipulate the serialized representation to create valid-looking containers with forged field values.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Deserialization attacks could inject malicious field values into trusted container structures.
